headline: Up Your Arsenal's PAL v1.00 code matching rises from 36.93% to 50.70%
summary: Up Your Arsenal's PAL v1.00 matched code rose from 36.93% to 50.70%. Its PAL v1.00 report counts 12,449 of 16,533 functions, while NTSC-U's separate report counts 12,145 of 16,528. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. Work across the vid-comics, multiplayer menu, campaign levels and engine libraries made this an unusually busy day for the early-stage branch.
highlights: Level work covers Starship Phoenix, Aquatos, Tyhrranosis, Kerwan, the final boss, Obani Draco and the Insomniac Museum, alongside shared code.
Build tools reproduce Sony compiler and assembler behavior and encrypt compiled DNAS blocks. Catalogue fixes distinguish actual functions from padding and encrypted data in the multiplayer menu.
Engine-library work includes memory allocation, formatted text, MPEG decoding and timer functions. The NTSC-U engine-core unit reached 156 of 178 functions, with remaining cases discussed in #67.
The replayed matching series was verified at its regenerated tip. Its author warns that the intermediate replay commits are not individually consistent or buildable.
Further level work opened in #65 for Annihilation Nation and other levels, #66 for shared level code, and #68 for level 23. All three remain unmerged.
#67 asks maintainers whether Sony library C may access the global-pointer register through a header. It is a proposal, not an approved expansion of the matching rules.
